judged_text: The migration string-interpolates each line of the migrated embeddable_hosts site setting directly into a raw SQL INSERT (VALUES ('#{h}', ...)), so a stored value containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL. The old embeddable_hosts setting was free-form admin-entered text with no write-side format validation (the removed allows_embeddable_host? only stripped schemes at read time, and the removed specs show values like 'http://discourse.org' being stored), so any value with an apostrophe aborts db:migrate with a PG syntax error and blocks the upgrade; a deliberately crafted setting value (config treated as attacker input) executes attacker-chosen SQL with the migration role's privileges during deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` (free-form text in prior versions) and is not escaped/quoted safely, any value containing a single quote will break the SQL and can potentially inject arbitrary SQL during migration. This is a real, diff-verifiable correctness/security issue that could block upgrades.
